blocks.text: 1. Function Calling
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862353-250293646.png

Tool Calling introduced the idea of defining available tools upfront with a name, purpose, and schema. Function Calling is the strict, schema-driven form that idea takes in most real model providers, the concrete interface an agent uses to invoke a specific function, and it closes out this Agentic RAG module.
It describes a function with a strict name and argument schema so the model can request it reliably.
2. Function Calling As A Concrete Implementation
Tool Calling names the general capability of a model requesting an external action, without running it itself.
Function calling is the specific, structured interface most model providers actually expose for that capability.

blocks.text: 3. A Strict JSON Schema Per Function

blocks.alt: A Strict JSON Schema Per Function
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862663-201985590.png
As with specifying an exact schema in JSON Output, each function is described with a strict JSON schema naming its parameters and their types.
The model's request is validated against that schema before anything runs.
4. The Model Outputs Arguments, Not Code

blocks.alt: The Model Outputs Arguments, Not Code
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862665-619920364.png
The model never writes or outputs executable code directly for a function call.
It only outputs the function name and a JSON object of arguments matching the schema.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A function call request naming get_order_status with the argument order_id set to A100 is just a JSON object, never a line of executable code the model wrote itself.

blocks.text: 5. Parallel Function Calls
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862665-621822857.png
As with decomposing a goal into steps in Planning, some model providers let a single response request several independent function calls at once.
Independent calls that do not depend on each other can run in parallel instead of one at a time.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Call pattern","Execution"],"rows":[["Sequential calls","One function call at a time, in order"],["Parallel calls","Independent calls run at the same time"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Handling A Function Call That Errors

blocks.alt: Handling A Function Call That Errors
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862666-63001879.png
As with an error in an early hop propagating forward in Multi-Hop RAG, a function call that fails or errors still needs its error fed back to the model.
Rather than the whole exchange silently breaking, feeding the error back gives the model a chance to recover.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A function call that raises an exception because an order ID does not exist should return an error message back to the model rather than crashing the whole conversation, letting the model try a different approach.

blocks.text: 7. Function Calling Versus General Tool Calling

blocks.alt: Function Calling Versus General Tool Calling
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862667-392023554.png
Tool calling can also cover looser mechanisms, like a model writing free text that a parser then interprets.
Function calling specifically means this strict, schema-validated request format.
8. Too Many Available Functions Confuses The Model
As with defining available tools upfront in Tool Calling, offering dozens of similarly named functions at once makes the right choice harder for the model.
A smaller, well-scoped function list improves how reliably the model picks correctly.
9. Recognizing When Strict Function Calling Earns Its Schema Overhead

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Strict Function Calling Earns Its Schema Overhead
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862667-490669255.png
Integrations with real external systems need function calling's strict validation.
A purely conversational assistant with no real actions to take, by contrast, never needs function calling at all.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Letting a function call proceed without validating its arguments against the schema first.
Crashing the whole conversation instead of feeding a function call error back to the model.
Offering dozens of similarly named functions at once instead of a smaller, well-scoped list.
Confusing function calling's strict schema format with looser, free-text tool calling mechanisms.

blocks.text: 12. Agentic RAG: Module Complete

items: Tool Calling: letting the model invoke a function with structured arguments, executed by the application.
Planning: sequencing multiple tool calls toward a goal before acting.
Reflection: evaluating whether a step's result, and the final answer, actually satisfied the goal.
Memory: retaining information across steps and conversations, filtered and kept current.
Multi-Agent Systems: several specialized agents coordinating toward a shared goal.
Dynamic Routing: choosing which agent or path to use per query at runtime.
Retrieval Planning: deciding the retrieval strategy for a query before executing any search.
Function Calling: the strict, schema-validated interface most providers use for tool calling.
Function calling describes each function with a strict JSON schema, validated before execution.
The model only outputs a function name and matching arguments, never executable code.
Independent function calls can run in parallel; failed calls should feed their error back, not crash.
Too many available functions makes it harder for the model to choose correctly.
This closes the Agentic RAG module; Graph RAG covers retrieval built on structured knowledge graphs next.
